geography.basis_note: 10-K revenue by geography: US $2,522.3m, UK $250.1m, Other countries $300.3m of $3,072.7m (computed shares, INFERENCE from FACT amounts). Verisk does not disclose North America/Europe/China; 'Other countries' bucket is not split. AR highlights: Domestic 82% / International 18%; subscription 83% / transactional 17%. ~70% of 2025 revenue from US P&C primary insurers.

claim_checks.finding: FY2025 10-K: US revenue $2,522.3m of $3,072.7m = 82.1% (company highlight 'Domestic 82%'); UK 8.1%; other countries 9.8%. Additional concentration: ~70% of 2025 revenue derived from US P&C primary insurers (10-K risk factor, p.19).

FY2025 OCC 6.6% (reported 6.6%); Q3 2026 OCC 7.4% (reported 5.3%); 9M 2026 OCC 6.0% (reported 4.5%). Record lacked history: OCC was 6.7/3.3/5.0 (2019-21, incl. since-divested Energy & FS), 6.5 (2022 continuing), 8.7 (2023), 7.1 (2024). Q1-Q2 2026 were below the 6-8% target; Q3 back in line.

claim_checks.claim: AI disintermediation evidence (record I1: claims/analytics exposed to AI-native competition)
claim_checks.finding: No quantified AI-driven churn disclosed. Q3-26 call: management frames AI as 'both opportunity and risk'; anecdote of a self-insured top-five retailer that brought workers' comp claims management in-house 'expecting AI to support the work' then returned to Verisk anti-fraud with a large multi-year deal (evidence that in-house AI substitution is being attempted by customers). Verisk is launching Forms AI Builder and MCP connectors for Anthropic Claude. Transactional OCC only +3.2% in Q3-26, attributed by management mainly to softening P&C markets, not AI. Evidence class: FACT (management statements) / INFERENCE (risk assessment).

claim_checks.claim: AccuLynx agreement terminated after FTC review (record corporate_actions)
claim_checks.finding: Q3-26 call (Nov-2026): CEO states the Delaware Supreme Court on 23-Oct-2026 affirmed the Chancery Court judgment and 'the transaction remains subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions and the FTC review' - i.e. the AccuLynx deal is live again (court-ordered), not definitively terminated. Leverage/capital-allocation assumptions should reflect possible completion.
